theater: 陝西寶雞陽平關與陳倉道

battle.name: 陽平關之戰
battle.theater: 陝西寶雞陽平關與陳倉道
battle.brief: 1236年夏，蒙古西路軍攻取興元（漢中）後沿陳倉道南下，兵臨陽平關。這道關隘卡在關中與漢中之間，是蒙古軍由西北插入四川的唯一車馬通道。宋將趙善據關死守，蒙古以壕溝、雲梯與遠射砲石強攻，關內弩砲與神臂弓居高壓制；關城終為蒙古軍所取，成都隨即洞開，蜀主孟昶出降。

kit.name: 十字弩
kit.history: 弩把射速交給了機械，代價是裝填慢。城牆上它比長弓可靠，野戰裡它比長弓脆弱。

countries: 交戰的雙方是蒙古帝國的西路軍與南宋的四川邊防軍。蒙古在1234年滅金之後，把關中與隴右一帶的降附軍府改編成進攻南宋的跳板，1235年窩闊台分兵三路伐宋：忽必烈取道荊襄，阿術與兀良合台經營兩淮，闊端與汪德臣領西路自陝西南下，圖取蜀地。這支部隊由蒙古本部騎兵、契丹與漢人降軍、色目攻城工匠以及金朝散兵拼成，編制上仍以千戶、百戶為骨幹，攻城則倚賴漢地匠戶與俘獲的守城工匠。1236年闊端病歿，兵權由汪德臣接手，軍紀與戰略一仍其舊。南宋方面，陽平關屬秦鳳路與鳳翔府防區，是川陝邊防體系中最北的一枚楔子，由朝廷直接任命的守將率禁軍與沿邊軍駐守，後方有興元、洋州、大散關與四川各州縣組成的梯次支撐。蒙古是主動進攻方，南宋是被動據隘方。同期還有第三方的存在：荊襄與兩淮的蒙古另兩路大軍，以及南宋在四川的援軍與地方團練，各路之間缺乏協同。
countriesEn: The two sides were the western army of the Mongol Empire and the Song frontier command holding Sichuan. After destroying Jin in 1234 the Mongols reorganised the surrendered administrations of Guanzhong and Longyou into a springboard for the war against Song. In 1235 Ögedei divided his forces into three columns: Kublai moved through Jing and Xiang, Ašu and Uriyangkhadai worked the country between the two Huai rivers, and Köden with Wang Dechen led the western column south from Shaanxi to take Shu. This army was pieced together from Mongol native cavalry, Khitan and Chinese surrendered troops, Uyghur and Muslim siege craftsmen and the scattered soldiers of Jin's last armies; its skeleton was still the thousand-man and hundred-man units, while the work of breaching walls was handed to Han Chinese engineers and to captured defenders. When Köden died of illness in 1236, command passed to Wang Dechen, who left both the discipline and the plan unchanged. On the Song side Yangping Pass belonged to the defence zone of Qinfeng circuit and Fengxiang prefecture and was the northernmost wedge of the Sichuan-Shaanxi frontier system, garrisoned by troops under officers appointed directly by the court, with a ladder of supporting posts behind it at Xingyuan, Yangzhou, Dasanguan and the Sichuan prefectures. The Mongols were the attacking party and the Song the garrison defending the defile. Third parties were present in the same year as well: the two other Mongol columns in Jingxiang and the Two Huai, together with Song reinforcements and local militia inside Sichuan, none of them well coordinated with the rest of the effort.
people: 蒙古方面的主將是汪德臣，鞏昌路人，早年歸附蒙古，通漢語、曉漢地山川形勢，1235年受命總兵陝西，負責關中與興元一線的軍政。1236年闊端病歿後，他實際統率西路軍攻略蜀地，是陽平關攻防中最主要的蒙古將領；其人用法近似漢地官僚，攻城先圖招降城中內應、驅迫俘囚填壕，深諳宋軍裝備與城防慣例，後來在1238年攻宋前線陣亡。西路統帥闊端為拖雷次子，1235年奉命經略關中，兵進隴右、招撫羌番，開闢了蒙古自關中入川的通道，惜在1236年一病不起，臨終仍以取蜀為念。南宋一方的守將是趙善，奉命屯守陽平關，是本戰役中宋軍的決策者；在城存糧盡、援兵不至的處境下，他力主固守而不許出降，左右指揮守城諸事，關於他最後的下落在傳世記載中並不一致。蒙古方面的漢地將佐與宋軍的守城將校，在史冊中多只以官職、隊將名目出現，難以逐一具名。金亡之後流落關中的詩人元好問，其詩文為這條戰線留下當時的側面記錄，可以與官修史書互證；川陝一線的堡寨屯戍官員與隨軍文士，也留下不少關於糧運、器械與城防的零星記載。
peopleEn: The principal Mongol commander was Wang Dechen, a native of Gongchang who had submitted to the Mongols early, spoke Chinese and knew the mountains and rivers of Han Chinese territory. In 1235 he was ordered to take charge of Shaanxi, handling the military and civil affairs of Guanzhong and the Xingyuan line. After Köden's death in 1236 he actually led the western column in the conquest of Shu and was the leading Mongol general at Yangping Pass. He governed in a manner close to that of a Han Chinese bureaucrat, always seeking surrender from insiders inside a city and driving captives to fill the ditches, and he understood Han Chinese equipment and the habits of Song city defence well; he was killed in 1238 on the Song front. The overall western commander, Köden, was a son of Tolui who in 1235 was ordered to govern Guanzhong. He pushed into Longyou and won over the Qiang and Tibetan groups, opening the road by which the Mongols entered Shu from the north-west, but he fell ill in 1236 and died with the taking of Shu still on his mind. The Song commander was Zhao Shan, ordered to hold Yangping Pass, and the decision maker of the Song defence. With grain running out and no relief arriving, he insisted on holding and refused any proposal to surrender, and he directed the defence in person, though the account of his own fate at the end is not consistent in the surviving records. Most Mongol Chinese commanders and Song garrison officers appear in the official histories only by rank or by company and cannot be named one by one. The poet Yuan Haowen, drifting in Guanzhong after the fall of Jin, left side-on records of this front in his verse that can be checked against the official histories; the officers of the forts and stations along the Sichuan-Shaanxi line and the civilian writers who followed the army also left scattered notes on grain supply, equipment and fortification.
kits: 這張卡上畫的是十字弩。弩是把弓弦交給機械去扣的武器：一端固定弓臂與弩機，射手只要扣下機括便可放弦，射程遠、命中比拉弓穩，缺點是裝填慢，一發之後必須重新上弦，無法像長弓那樣連珠射擊。12世紀的歐亞兩端都在使用同一原理的弩：歐洲是帶蹺蹬的十字弩，東亞則是形制更繁多的弩，張弦方式從蹶張、踏張到絞盤各不相同。陽平關的戰場上，實際起作用的是宋軍那一整套弩兵裝備。體量最小的是臂弩，單兵可攜，射速略勝於弓而射程約在百步上下；主力是蹶張弩，以人力踏張，需要結實士卒輪流操作，箭矢粗重，穿透力強。守城最倚重的是神臂弓一類的踏張大弩，張弦要靠數人合力的張弩架或絞車，射出的箭矢重達數斤，據《宋史·兵志》所記，其射程遠達五百步，強弩更可及七百步，居高臨下可以覆蓋關前的坡道、壕溝與攻城器械所在。此外還有架在城頭的弩砲與床弩，發射大矢或石彈，是對付雲梯與衝撞器械的最後一道火線。宋軍在城頭還備有檑石、油鍋、撞竿、鐵蒺藜與拒馬，弓弩之間以矢石相濟。蒙古軍這邊以蒙古弓為主，彎弓輕捷、騎射自幼訓練，攻城時使用雲梯、覆以濕牛皮的攻城槌、繩索攀援、掘進的壕溝與遠射石砲；狹窄的陳倉道不利於展開大型攻城器械，這正是蒙古軍不得不倚重繩梯與強攻、宋軍得以死守的原因之一。
kitsEn: The card shows a crossbow. A crossbow hands the drawing of the string over to a mechanism: the bow arm and its trigger are fixed at one end, and the archer only has to work the trigger to release the string. Its range is longer and its aim steadier than that of a bow, but loading is slow, and after a single shot the string must be restrung, so it cannot fire in the rapid sequence a longbow allows. The twelfth century used the same mechanical principle at both ends of Eurasia: in Europe the stirrup crossbow, in East Asia a far more varied family of crossbows whose strings were drawn by the feet, by the legs or by windlasses. What actually fought at Yangping Pass was the whole crossbow establishment of the Song army. The smallest was the hand crossbow, carried by a single soldier, slightly quicker than a bow and with a range of roughly a hundred paces. The main body was the treadle crossbow, strung by the legs and needing strong men working in turn, firing heavy bolts with real penetration. The most important for the defence was the large treadle crossbow of the shenbi type, whose string required several men working a draw-stand or a windlass; its bolts weighed several catties, and the History of Song in its treatise on the army records a range of five hundred paces, the powerful crossbow reaching seven hundred, which from above could cover the approach slopes, the ditches and the ground where the siege machines stood. On the walls were also crossbow catapults and bed crossbows firing heavy bolts or stone shot, the last line against ladders and battering rams. The Song garrison further kept hanging stones, boiling oil, ramming poles, iron caltrops and spiked barriers, mixing arrows with stones and shot. The Mongols fought mainly with the Mongol composite bow, light and quick and drilled into their riders from childhood, and for the siege used ladders, hides-covered rams, ropes for climbing, sapping and trench work and stone-throwing engines. The narrow Chencang road gave them little room to deploy large engines, which is one reason they had to rely on rope ladders and assault while the Song could hold on.
tactics: 蒙古軍的攻城思路是草原式圍城加上漢地式工程。兵到之後先取興元、洋州等沿線城寨，使陽平關成為孤立的突出部；然後合圍關城，只留一面通給養，同時派騎兵巡邏四野，斷絕關內與南面的聯繫，等待援軍或糧援自行崩潰。攻城本身分作數路：一路在遠處以弓弩與遠射砲壓制城頭，一路在夜裡以雲梯、繩索貼近牆面，一路挖掘地道、壕溝，把接近通道逐步填平。傳世詩文與記錄中屢見城頭徹夜擊鼓、點燃火把虛張援兵之勢的描寫，說明守軍在資訊不明的情況下習慣用聲光拖延敵人的判斷。宋軍的部署則是典型的隘口防守：主力壓在關城南面與兩側山脊，弓弩分層配置，遠射交由神臂弓與弩砲擔當，近射以步弓、弩手在城垛口射擊；關前的坡道上挖壕、埋蒺藜、置拒馬，兩翼山梁設烽燧與遊騎，使蒙古騎兵無法展開。陳倉道狹窄，蒙古的騎兵優勢難以發揮，只能化整為零下馬攻關，這一點同時限制雙方：蒙古失去速度，宋軍失去援護。最後決定戰局的不是一場決戰，而是糧道。蒙古若不能在關下速勝，關中後方的糧草供應就會把戰線拉長；宋軍援兵若在半路被截斷，關城也會在孤立中耗盡。
tacticsEn: The Mongol approach was the classic steppe siege combined with Chinese engineering. On arrival they first took the line posts at Xingyuan and Yangzhou, leaving Yangping Pass an isolated salient. They then ringed the pass, leaving a single opening for supplies, while cavalry patrolled the open country and cut the pass off from the south, waiting for relief armies or grain convoys to collapse of their own accord. The assault was divided into several parts: one line engaged the wall from a distance with bows and stone-throwing engines, one scaled the walls at night with ladders and ropes, and one dug saps and ditches, gradually filling in the approaches. Contemporary poems and records repeatedly describe beating drums through the night and lighting torches on the walls to make relief troops seem present, which shows how a garrison short of information used sound and firelight to slow the enemy's judgement. The Song deployment was a typical defence of a defile. The main strength sat on the southern face of the pass and on the ridges to either side, with bows and crossbows layered, long range work given to the shenbi crossbows and the crossbow catapults, and close range work to foot bows and crossbowmen firing from the crenellations. On the approach slope the Song dug ditches, laid caltrops and set spiked barriers, and on the flanking hillsides they lit beacon fires and posted mounted patrols so that Mongol cavalry could not deploy. The Chencang road was too narrow for the Mongol horse to manoeuvre, so the riders had to dismount and attack, and this limited both sides: the Mongols lost speed and the Song lost the cover of mobile troops. What finally decided the matter was not a single battle but the grain route. If the Mongols could not win quickly below the pass, the supply line from Guanzhong would lengthen the whole operation; and if the Song relief army was intercepted on the way, the pass would run out of strength while isolated.
data: 可用的數字大致可以擺出這樣幾組。時間上，1234年蒙古滅金，1235年秋分三路伐宋，1236年夏西路軍攻取興元（漢中），同年冬蒙古軍進入成都、蜀主孟昶出降，從滅金到平蜀只用兩年多，攻勢節奏相當緊湊。路程上，興元到陽平關沿山道約二百餘里，車馬運糧在雨季需十餘日，後方補給線的長度直接限制了圍城的時限。城防方面，陽平關依陳倉道與斜谷交會處的丘壑而建，關垣連亘數里，前有陡坡與壕溝，關後即陳倉川的狹窄谷地，可供展開的平地極少。武器數據常被後人引用的是《宋史·兵志》那一段：弓射二百步，弩射三百步，神臂弓射五百步，強弩射七百步；神臂弓所發箭矢重約三斤，一具之價約合錢一千五百，宋人以此強調其耗費；守城重裝步人甲約二十九斤一副，弩手多披札甲或布背甲。蒙古西路軍的兵數，史料多只說數萬之眾，沒有更細的分營記載，可以核實的只有它必須分兵維持關中、興元與南方三處的補給。關於宋軍守關兵力的確切數目，現存材料無從確證，只能依城制與糧載量推知，規模在數千至一萬之間。傷亡與攻城器械耗損的數字，流傳記載多有誇大或互有出入，不宜當作準確依據。
dataEn: The usable figures can be set out roughly as follows. In time: the Mongols destroyed Jin in 1234, divided into three columns for the attack on Song in the autumn of 1235, took Xingyuan (Hanzhong) with the western army in the summer of 1236, and entered Chengdu in the winter of the same year, when the Shu ruler Meng Chang surrendered. It took barely two years to go from the fall of Jin to the conquest of Shu, which shows how tight the offensive rhythm was. In distance: the mountain road from Xingyuan to Yangping Pass is about two hundred li, and grain moved by cart and pack animal needed more than ten days in the rainy season, so the length of the supply line set a hard limit on how long the siege could last. As for the works: Yangping Pass was built on the hummocks where the Chencang road meets the Xie valley, its walls running for several li, with a steep slope and a ditch in front and the narrow valley of the Chencang stream behind, leaving almost no open ground to deploy on. The weapon figures most often quoted come from the History of Song and its treatise on the army: the bow reaches two hundred paces, the crossbow three hundred, the shenbi crossbow five hundred and the powerful crossbow seven hundred. The bolt of a shenbi crossbow weighed about three catties and one set cost about fifteen hundred cash, a point the Song used to stress the expense. The heavy infantry armour of the Song weighed about twenty-nine catties a set, and crossbowmen generally wore lamellar armour or cloth-backed armour. The strength of the Mongol western column is given in the sources only as some tens of thousands, with no detailed breakdown by camp; the only certain point is that it had to keep forces in three places at once, supplying Guanzhong, Xingyuan and the south. The exact number of Song troops in the pass cannot be established from what survives and can only be inferred from the size of the works and the carrying capacity of the granaries, on a scale of several thousand to ten thousand. Figures for casualties and for the wastage of siege equipment are often exaggerated or inconsistent from record to record and should not be treated as exact.
cause: 這場戰爭的直接起因，是蒙古在滅金之後需要一個新方向。1234年初蔡州陷落、金朝滅亡，蒙古與南宋的邊界立刻拉成從東北到西北的一條長線，南宋拒絕繼續輸送歲幣，1235年窩闊台以此為口實分兵三路大舉攻宋，西路取蜀是其中關鍵的一著。從蒙古的角度看，蜀地是南宋西部最厚的屏障，掌握四川便等於取得進攻兩湖與長江中游的縱深，同時可以西接雲南的兀良合台部，形成對南宋的鉗形；先取漢中、再取成都，是最省力的次序。從南宋的角度看，川陝一線的關隘是四塞中的最後一道門戶，成都平原與上游的糧源全靠它遮蔽，因此朝廷寧可傾力增援也不能讓陽平關破。至於陽平關本身被盯上的原因，則是純粹的地理：它卡在陳倉道上，北接鳳翔與京兆，南抵興元，是關中與漢中之間唯一能通行車馬的通道；只要守住它，蒙古的西路軍就無法從西北直接插入蜀地，必須繞道或強攻。蒙古軍的到來本身也帶著軍事之外的理由：草原帝國剛剛滅掉鄰邦，需要新的戰場與新的分利管道，而南宋的四川正是最薄弱的一塊。
causeEn: The immediate cause of this war was that the Mongols needed a new direction after the fall of Jin. When Cai Prefecture fell in the first month of 1234 and Jin was destroyed, the border between the Mongols and Song instantly became a long line running from the north-east to the north-west. Song refused to continue paying the annual tribute, and in 1235 Ögedei used that as a pretext to launch a three-pronged invasion, in which taking Shu by the western route was the essential move. From the Mongol point of view Shu was the thickest shield the Song still had in the west: to hold Sichuan was to gain depth for an attack on the middle Yangtze and the Two Lakes, and to connect with Uriyangkhadai in Yunnan so as to form pincers against Song. Taking Hanzhong first and Chengdu second was the shortest order of operations. From the Song point of view the passes on the Sichuan-Shaanxi line were the last of the four frontiers, and the grain of the Chengdu plain and the upper river depended on them for cover, so the court was ready to pour in reinforcements rather than let Yangping Pass fall. Yangping Pass itself was singled out for purely geographical reasons: it sits on the Chencang road between Guanzhong and Hanzhong, joins Fengxiang and Jingzhao to the north with Xingyuan to the south, and is the only route on which carts and horses can pass. Hold it, and the western column cannot drive straight into Shu from the north-west; it must go round or force it. The arrival of the Mongol army in turn carried reasons beyond the military alone: the steppe empire had just destroyed its neighbour and now needed fresh theatres and fresh channels of profit, and the Song's Sichuan was the thinnest place in which to find them.
impact: 這場戰役的結果，改變了南宋西部的整個戰局。蒙古軍突破陳倉道之後，興元失守，成都門戶洞開，蜀主孟昶出降，數百年的蜀國就此終結，南宋在西部失去了成片的藩籬。成都隨後成為蒙古西路軍的基地，從關中運來的糧草、從雲南來的物資與從中亞來的工匠在這裡匯合，後來對釣魚城、合州、夔州與長江中游的持久圍城，技術與物資都靠此地支撐。對南宋而言，失蜀不只是少了一層屏障，更直接動搖了它的財政：四川是軍糧與軍餉的重要來源，進口軍馬與貨物的通道也斷了。朝廷此後對守重於攻的爭論、對賈似道等人主張持重與依賴江淮的策略，都因此添了分量。兵器層面的教訓同樣清楚：守城一方有神臂弓、弩砲這樣的利器，卻擋不住拋石、壕溝與長期圍困，說明遠射武器再強也不能替代城牆、糧秣與援軍；而攻城一方第一次在中國西南山區系統地運用漢地攻城術與回回工匠，也把山道奪取的難度變成可以估算的問題。這種工程經驗一路積累到後來攻襄陽與攻四川的山地戰役上，成為蒙古最終滅宋的技術底子。
impactEn: The outcome of this campaign redrew the whole western front of the Song war. Once the Mongols broke through the Chencang road, Xingyuan fell, Chengdu was left open, the Shu ruler Meng Chang surrendered, and a state that had lasted for centuries was brought to an end; the Song lost a whole shield in the west. Chengdu then became the base of the Mongol western army, where grain from Guanzhong, goods from Yunnan and craftsmen from Central Asia converged, and it was from there that the later prolonged sieges of Diaoyucheng, Hezhou, Kuizhou and the middle Yangtze drew their materiel and their technical support. For the Song the loss of Shu was not merely the loss of a barrier: Sichuan was an important source of military grain and military pay, and the channel for imported warhorses and trade goods was cut with it. The later debate at court over holding rather than attacking, and the arguments of people like Jia Sidao for caution and for reliance on the Yangtze and the Two Huai, both gained weight from it. The lesson about weapons was equally clear. A defending side with shenbi crossbows and crossbow catapults still could not hold off stone-throwing engines, trenches and a long siege, which showed that no ranged weapon, however powerful, replaces walls, grain and relief troops. For the attacking side, the first systematic use in the mountains of south-west China of Chinese siege technique and Muslim engineers turned the difficulty of mountain roads into a problem that could be estimated. This engineering experience accumulated down to the later sieges of Xiangyang and the mountain campaigns in Sichuan, becoming the technical foundation of the final destruction of Song.
result: 就戰術層面說，陽平關沒有守住。蒙古西路軍在攻取興元之後，把主力壓到關下，圍城曠日持久，關內糧援俱絕，宋軍的守勢在蒙古持續不斷的壕溝、梯砲與夜襲之下逐步崩解，關城最終為蒙古軍所取，陳倉道自此洞開，宋人在西北的門戶轉為蒙古人的進軍通道。關於陷落時的最後一幕，傳世記載殘缺而互有出入：有的說守軍力戰至破，有的說城中糧盡議降而為主將所拒；可以確定的是蒙古軍最終取得了陽平關，宋軍未能把守勢維持到底，趙善等守將的最後去向，在不同記錄中說法不一。更大的成果則在關外：蒙古軍在同年秋冬季推進至成都，蜀主孟昶奉表出降，川西盡入蒙古版圖。從全局看，這是1235年三路伐宋中最見成效的一路，蒙古由此獲得西部戰爭的縱深與補給基地，而南宋則退守江淮、兩湖與四川沿線的殘餘據點。此後蒙古的注意力轉向荊襄與釣魚城，陽平關則成為蒙古在關中的固定屯兵與轉運節點，直到元代仍是西北對蜀作戰的後方。
resultEn: At the tactical level Yangping Pass was not held. After taking Xingyuan, the Mongol western column pressed its main strength against the pass and the siege dragged on for months. Inside the walls grain and relief both ran out, and the Song position gradually collapsed under continuous trenching, ladders, stone-throwing engines and night attacks, until the pass fell to the Mongols. The Chencang road was open from that moment onward, and what had been a Song gateway in the north-west became a Mongol avenue of approach. The last moments of the fall are fragmentary and inconsistent: some accounts speak of the garrison fighting to the end, others of a debate inside the city to surrender that the commander refused. What can be certain is that the Mongols finally took the pass and that the Song could not hold the position to the end, and that the last fate of Zhao Shan and the other commanders is described differently from record to record. The larger results lay outside the walls: in the autumn and winter of the same year the Mongol army pressed on to Chengdu, the Shu ruler Meng Chang presented himself in surrender, and western Sichuan passed entirely under Mongol rule. In the wider view this was the most successful of the three columns of 1235, giving the Mongols depth in the west and a supply base, while the Song fell back on its remaining posts along the Yangtze, the Two Huai, the Two Lakes and the edge of Sichuan. Mongol attention then turned to Jingxiang and to Diaoyucheng, while Yangping Pass became a fixed garrison and transfer point for the Mongols in Guanzhong, remaining a rear base for operations against Shu into the Yuan period.
